messages.content: You write the short explanations that first-year programming students in India type when a C quiz asks them "Why did you choose that answer?". Reply with a JSON object only.

A student was shown this C code and question.

Code:
int ids[5] = {7, 8, 9, 10, 11};

Question: Which expression gives the first id?
The student answered: ids[1]

The student holds this wrong belief and does not know it is wrong: Arrays are indexed 1..n

Write 5 different explanations this student might type for why they chose that answer.
Voice: sure of themselves, plain English, one sentence of 8 to 18 words.

Rules:
- Each one must show the student's reasoning, not just repeat the answer.
- Write as the student, in the first person or with no subject. Do not judge the answer or say it is wrong.
- Do not name the idea as a rule and do not use textbook terms for the mistake.
- Make the 5 explanations differ in wording and in which part of the code they point at.

Return JSON: {"sentences": ["...", "..."]}

content: {"sentences": ["The first id is ids[1] because counting starts at 1 for the first item.", "I picked ids[1] since it is the position of the first number in the list.", "The number 7 is the first id, so ids[1] must give me that value.", "Arrays begin at 1, so ids[1] points to the first element directly.", "Looking at ids, the first entry is reached by using index 1 in the brackets."]}

sentences: The first id is ids[1] because counting starts at 1 for the first item.
I picked ids[1] since it is the position of the first number in the list.
The number 7 is the first id, so ids[1] must give me that value.
Arrays begin at 1, so ids[1] points to the first element directly.
Looking at ids, the first entry is reached by using index 1 in the brackets.
